small_guidance:
- The post-conv fused kernel is already cheap; the ConvTranspose2d dominates the 22ms runtime. Tuning BLOCK_C/num_warps on the existing fused kernel will not close the gap to the 12ms baseline (which uses cuDNN's optimized transposed conv).
- If staying with torch's conv_transpose, try `channels_last` memory format for the conv input/weight to let cuDNN pick a faster algorithm, and keep the fused epilogue as-is (perhaps bump num_warps to 4 for BLOCK_C=128).
- Ensure the bias load is hoisted/broadcast-friendly: with C=128 and HW=128*128, the kernel launches ~2M programs each loading 128 channels — consider tiling multiple (h,w) per program to amortize bias loads.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.ConvTranspose2d` with a custom Triton scatter-add kernel: for each input element `x[n, ic, ih, iw]`, scatter `x * W[ic, oc, :, :]` into the output grid at the corresponding strided/padded location. This is the high-headroom move since cuDNN's transposed conv is the bottleneck (~22ms vs 12ms baseline implies the conv is most of the cost).
- Alternatively, implement transposed conv as a gather-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile), iterating over (ic, kh, kw) and gathering the appropriate input element (with stride/padding inversion: `ih = (oh + padding - kh) / stride` when divisible). Fuse softmax-bias-scale-sigmoid into the epilogue — though softmax requires a channel reduction so it must come after the full OC is computed; consider two kernels: (1) custom conv_transpose writing to a buffer, (2) existing fused epilogue.
- Use channels-last layout (N, H, W, C) end-to-end so the softmax-along-C reduction and the conv's OC accumulation both have contiguous channel access; this also helps the bias broadcast.
